groups.defect: The relaxed isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) guard no longer requires that no user is selected yet. So per-user WebAuthn data (it shows that passkeys exist and can include credential IDs via passkeys.ftl) is now filled into pages served to a visitor who has only typed a username. That reveals that the account exists and has passkeys. Suggested fix: allow this only during re-authentication (USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH).

answer.reasoning: Both suggestions report the same disclosure with the same root cause: the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled guard drops the old context.getUser()==null condition, so per-user passkey or credential data reaches visitors who have not authenticated. Both propose the same fix: allow it only when USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is set. s_28120ad1 points at UsernamePasswordForm.challenge. s_fb963067 points at PasswordForm.render and also names UsernamePasswordForm.challenge lines 137-140, so it already covers both locations. Both call sites use the same helper, so one change to the gating fixes both. That makes this cross_location. needsUnifiedComment is false because s_fb963067 already covers both places. That last point is a minor judgment call, but the grouping itself is clear.
